answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. Consider a relic as the anchor of the cost. A opal stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ferrous hold...
